analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md (documentation). Two edits are visible in the file_changes patch: (1) a new paragraph after the update section (head lines ~1804-1810) stating that after `darkbloom update` on a Mac running `darkbloom cluster`, the command asks the cluster service supervisor to restart into the installed release with the other Mac after a drain, bounded by `--timeout`; a deferral exits 1. (2) The `auto_update` config row now mentions coordinated pair updates (head line 2148). The supplied units (head lines 795-1694) are unchanged surrounding documentation: add-on hold, sandbox setup/installer, stop/restart/status/doctor and models commands. I checked them against the threat model, including TB-013/T-061 (sandbox installer is TLS-only on the CLI side, and the installer verifies the release), TB-012 (add-on hold), TB-011 (App Attest on restart), and T-041 (prefix cache). No security control or code is changed, and the docs I saw make no new unsafe claims. The docs describe the existing installer download constraints: HTTPS-only, 1 MiB limit, 0600 file in a 0700 directory, and a documented note that the CLI itself does not verify the script. That is consistent with T-061. Remaining integration questions, not findings: the cluster-update code (UpdateCommand.swift, ClusterServiceUpdateRequest) and the cluster-service supervisor are not in the supplied evidence. The threat model has no entry for the new cluster-coordinated update/restart path or for how the supervisor authenticates the restart request and the peer Mac. If the corresponding code lands in a separate PR, it should be reviewed for a possible new trust boundary. The update path still verifies bundle, binary and metallib hashes per the unchanged text. Only the doc text is evidenced here.
